text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- President Aleksander Kwasniewski must decide by Wednesday whether to sign parliament's vetting bill, aimed at revealing former security police informers who seek public posts. He criticised the bill for lacking clear definition of what constituted a secret informer and for failing to provide mechanisms to allow citizens to see their files.
ZYCIE

- Marian Pilka is expected to stand down as Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) deputy chairman on Thursday. The Coordination Committee formed by the liberal conservative wing of AWS has also demanded the resignation of board members Janusz Tomaszewski and Adam Slomka.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Business Centre Club (BCC) has awarded 15 leading companies so-called diamond awards for their financial results and charity and environment protection activities. Among others, the firms include Animex, Convector, Exbud, Pollena Ewa, Drumet, Lech Browary Wielkopolski, TC Debica, Metalexport and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK).
- The KGHM copper conglomerate plans to invest $54 million in copper and cobalt mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the former Zaire, to start next year, the firm said.
- Sweden has permitted Poland to spend $6.5 million, two percent of the debt owed by Poland, on environment protection schemes inside the country.

- The IBCA rating agency has lowered the long-term rating of the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) from BBB- to BB+ and its legal rating from 4 to 2. The decision was a result of the bank's privatisation a few weeks ago.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.5 percent in 1998 and inflation will range between 9.0 percent and 9.5 percent, the cabinet's economic ministers' committee (KERM) said.

- The Huta Katowice steel mill will apply for arbitrage by the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in response to the introduction of anti-dumping customs duties by Thailand against Polish steel exports, the plant's spokesperson Renata Bytomska said.
- Poland's outdoor advertising firms operate 40,000 billboards around the country, a report by the Outdoor Advertising Association said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poles spent 3.8 billion zlotys on insurance in the first quarter of 1997, showing significant growth compared with 2.6 billion zlotys spent on policies in the same period last year, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- South Korea's Samsung Finance Group, interested in the purchase of the Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK), has protested against the government's decision to permit altering the offer by a Polish financial group including Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH), the Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR) Polish Development Bank, Kredyt Bank and the Warta insurance firm.
PARKIET
- The net profit of Poland's banking sector declined by 11.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year, a report by GUS said.
- Denmark's NTK Cables now holds a 51 percent stake in the listed Slaska Fabryka Kabli (SFK) cable maker, SFK's president Tadeusz Polok said.
- Two glass makers, Huta Szkla Ujscie and Huta Szkla Orzesze are planning to merge into one capital group, they said.
NOTE
- Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
